title: The Burning Cauldron of Fiery Fire by Anne Washburn at Vineyard Theat...
transcript: Anne Washburn's new play The Burning Cauldron of Fiery Fire will probably be just as polarizing as her 2013 play Mr. Burns. This one, currently running at Vineyard, is a tender and comical but kind of unsettling story about death and community. Set in Northern California, the inciting event is that someone unexpectedly dies within a remote and mostly off the grid community — a fascinating premise, and this play does not hold your hand through it. You definitely have to lean in, and even with the piece keeping my full attention, there were still moments that I straight up did not understand, but that's okay. Things get especially blurry in Act 2 when the narrative skews a bit, though the themes paradoxically begin to emerge with more clarity. And I think the potential divisiveness of this piece comes from whether or not you feel like it's alienating you or inviting you to pick it apart and piece it back together. I'm still figuring it out, but I definitely enjoyed the performances, the scenic design, and the incredible puppetry. I also enjoyed its generally mysterious tone and the moments of unexpectedly poetic writing that speak to the broader ideas of individualism and capitalism versus collectivism and community. The play is still in previews, so I'm patiently awaiting more audience reception as I'm super curious about the interpretations that folks will have. With that, another program for my collection.
